claims.text: A circuit breaker (Polly) watches the outcomes of calls and, once too many fail, opens: calls are then rejected at once without executing the wrapped call, until a break duration passes.
claims.source_hint: Polly docs: Strategies > Circuit breaker (overview, 'Defaults' and state diagram)

claims.text: Polly breaker states: Closed (calls pass, outcomes sampled), Open (calls rejected with BrokenCircuitException); the first call after BreakDuration moves it to HalfOpen and passes as a trial (success closes it, failure reopens it for another BreakDuration). No manual action needed.
claims.source_hint: Polly docs: Strategies > Circuit breaker, 'Circuit breaker state' / state diagram

claims.text: Polly's circuit breaker opens when, within SamplingDuration, the failure ratio is at least FailureRatio and the number of calls is at least MinimumThroughput; BreakDuration is how long it stays open before half-open.
claims.source_hint: Polly docs: Strategies > Circuit breaker, CircuitBreakerStrategyOptions (FailureRatio, MinimumThroughput, SamplingDuration, BreakDuration)

claims.text: HttpCircuitBreakerStrategyOptions (Microsoft.Extensions.Http.Resilience) handles by default: HttpRequestException, TimeoutRejectedException, and responses with status 5xx, 408 (Request Timeout) or 429 (Too Many Requests); other answers, such as 200 or 422, are not counted as failures.
claims.source_hint: Microsoft Learn: Build resilient HTTP apps / HttpCircuitBreakerStrategyOptions, HttpClientResiliencePredicates.IsTransient; RFC 9110 §15.5.9 (408), RFC 6585 §4 (429)

claims.text: Strategies run in the order added, the first added outermost: the breaker added before AddTimeout wraps the timeout and sees TimeoutRejectedException as the call's outcome, counting it as failed.
claims.source_hint: Polly docs: Resilience pipelines, strategy order; examples/don-hang @ stage-3: DonHang.Payments/Program.cs lines 89-96, 113, 124

claims.text: While the circuit is open, the circuit breaker strategy throws BrokenCircuitException (Polly.CircuitBreaker) instead of executing the call, so no request reaches the HttpClient's primary handler.
claims.source_hint: Polly docs: Strategies > Circuit breaker, BrokenCircuitException; examples/don-hang @ stage-3: GatewayCircuitBreakerTests.cs lines 67-82

claims.text: GatewayRefundClient.RefundAsync @ stage-3 catches BrokenCircuitException (lines 82-85) and TimeoutRejectedException (lines 78-81) and returns RefundOutcome.TryAgainLater; 422 returns Refused. fake-gateway answers 422 to bank_transfer refunds.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-3: DonHang.Payments/GatewayRefundClient.cs lines 66-85; fake-gateway/Program.cs lines 93-94

claims.text: Program.cs @ stage-3 107-125: AddCircuitBreaker(HttpCircuitBreakerStrategyOptions) at 113, four settings from gateway (the GatewaySettings parameter), OnOpened/OnHalfOpened/OnClosed logging via the Log helper below (it only runs the write), AddTimeout at 124.
OnOpened, OnHalfOpened and OnClosed are callbacks of Polly's CircuitBreakerStrategyOptions invoked on each state change; OnOpened's arguments expose BreakDuration.
claims.source_hint: Polly docs: Strategies > Circuit breaker, CircuitBreakerStrategyOptions events (OnCircuitOpenedArguments.BreakDuration)

claims.text: GatewaySettings @ stage-3 defaults: FailureRatio 0.5, MinimumThroughput 3, SamplingDuration 1 minute, BreakDuration 30 s, Timeout 10 s; docker-compose.yml sets Gateway__BreakDuration "00:00:10" for payments, so the lab's break is 10 s.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-3: DonHang.Payments/GatewayRefundClient.cs lines 27-36; docker-compose.yml line 380

claims.text: A MinimumThroughput higher than the number of calls RefundSender sends within SamplingDuration would keep the circuit closed through an outage; it is set low when the caller sends few calls.
claims.source_hint: Polly docs: Strategies > Circuit breaker, MinimumThroughput

claims.text: A call refused by the open circuit is, for RefundSender, a failed attempt: the row stays pending and is scheduled again with backoff, until RefundSender's give-up time since the request has passed (RefundSender.cs line 99).

GatewayCircuitBreakerTests @ stage-3: three 500 answers then a fourth call returns TryAgainLater with 'circuit' in the reason and the fake handler counts 3 calls; five 422 refusals all reach the handler (5 calls); after BreakDuration a successful trial closes the circuit.

circuit-breaker.sh @ stage-3 restarts payments (breaker counts are in memory), stops fake-gateway, POSTs /api/v1/orders/10/refund, prints attempts and the breaker's log, starts fake-gateway and waits until order 10 is cancelled, the order's status once its refund succeeds.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-3: scripts/backend/circuit-breaker.sh lines 25-66; scripts/lib/refunds.sh wait_for_status

claims.text: Captured output @ stage-3: 202; attempts 1-3 'the call failed', attempt 4 'not sent, the circuit is open'; 'Circuit to the gateway opened: no calls for 10 s'; after 'fake-gateway is back': half-open then closed lines.
Counting 422 refusals as failures would let a few refusals open the circuit and make refunds the gateway would accept fail at once; a refusal means the gateway is up.
A retry repeats one call after it fails, while a circuit breaker never repeats a call and only decides whether new calls are sent.
claims.source_hint: Polly docs: Strategies > Retry vs Circuit breaker overviews
